einzeiler: Film Forum staff discuss Francis Ford Coppola's eclectic 25-film retrospective.
kurzfassung: Staff members at Film Forum explore the diverse filmography of Francis Ford Coppola ahead of a major retrospective. The episodes highlight lesser-seen works, experimental genre films, and his ambitious productions from the 1960s to today. The hosts examine how Coppola continuously reinvented his style, moving from legendary mob dramas to deeply personal independent projects.
stichpunkte: Film Forum hosts a 25-film retrospective dedicated to Francis Ford Coppola, running from August 21 to September 10.
The 1970s cemented Coppola's legacy with masterworks like The Godfather, The Conversation, The Godfather Part II, and Apocalypse Now.
Early works like the 1963 horror film Dementia 13 showcase his beginnings under producer Roger Corman.
The eclectic post-70s run includes ambitious box-office gambles like One from the Heart and stylistically distinct films like Rumblefish.
Late-career and post-retirement projects such as Twixt and Youth Without Youth reflect deeply personal themes and digital experimentation.
Staff members share personal connections to lesser-known titles, discussing their unique tonal shifts and narrative structures.
Coppola's persistent fascination with live cinema culminates in his long-gestating passion project Megalopolis.

clips.hook: Four films, four Best Picture nominees, two winners.
clips.text: The hosts recap Coppola's phenomenal run in the 1970s, noting how every single feature released during that decade earned a Best Picture nomination.

clips.hook: The worst movie to ever make you cry.
clips.text: One speaker describes Twixt as a chaotic viewing experience that nonetheless packs an unexpected emotional punch at the very end.

clips.hook: You got to be bad just to have a good time.
clips.text: A staff member compares the rebellious, small-town nihilism of Rumblefish to an old Texas saying about youthful delinquency.

clips.hook: If you were a once world-beating conquering director, what do you do today?
clips.text: The discussion turns to how Coppola navigated the 1990s by taking on diverse projects like legacy sequels, high-concept star vehicles, and literary adaptations.

clips.hook: The building inspector came in one day, said, what are these wires?
clips.text: Bruce Goldstein recalls an anecdote about wiring theater seats for William Castle's gimmick horror film The Tingler before authorities intervened.

beschreibung: Welcome to Lobby Talk, a new podcast series from Film Forum Presents. At Film Forum, the theaters are where you experience cinema - but the lobby is where you truly begin to engage with and make sense of cinema. Lobby Talk celebrates this magical space that has provoked over 55 years of conversation, good-humored disagreement, and impassioned hot takes. In these episodes, the die-hard movie people on staff at Film Forum weigh in on the upcoming programming they're excited about, and you'll also meet special guests that happen to be passing through the lobby. In this, our inaugural episode, we will be talking about COPPOLA, the exciting 25-film series devoted to beloved auteur Francis Ford Coppola, running August 20 - September 10.
